raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

  The filesystem KV offloading tier currently uses a single storage path and assumes direct I/O can be selected for an entire batch. This PR adds two capabilities to the filesystem KV offloading tier:

  - Optional whole-block sharding across an ordered, comma-separated list of storage paths using `path_sharding: "by_block_hash"`. Blocks assigned to different paths are processed in parallel, while existing single-path behavior remains unchanged.
  - Safe O_DIRECT selection based on per-path support and per-operation buffer and length alignment. Unaligned operations fall back to buffered I/O.

Documentation is included for the new configuration and block-placement behavior.

  ## Test Plan

  Focused unit tests:

  ```bash
  python -m pytest tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_fs_tier.py
  ```

  Multi-path filesystem KV offloading configuration:

  ```bash
  kv_transfer_config='{
    "kv_connector": "OffloadingConnector",
    "kv_role": "kv_both",
    "kv_connector_extra_config": {
      "spec_name": "TieringOffloadingSpec",
      "cpu_bytes_to_use": 34359738368,
      "block_size": 1024,
      "eviction_policy": "lru",
      "secondary_tiers": [{
        "type": "fs",
        "root_dir": "/mnt/ps-1/kv-cache,/mnt/ps-2/kv-cache,/mnt/ps-3/kv-cache,/mnt/ps-4/kv-cache",
        "path_sharding": "by_block_hash",
        "n_read_threads": 64,
        "n_write_threads": 64
      }]
    }
  }'

  vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct \
    --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --max-model-len 262144 \
    --no-enable-prefix-caching \
    --kv-transfer-config "$kv_transfer_config"
  ```
  
 ## Test Result

  The native extension was rebuilt from source against CUDA 13 on H100 using an editable installation. The focused unit tests were rerun against the rebuilt extension.

  Runtime validation used four filesystem paths with TP=4 and a 128K-token request. Three storage-hit reads retrieved all `126/126` requested blocks without short-I/O or backend errors.

  The four-paths configuration reduced mean storage-hit TTFT by **41.1%**. Mean filesystem-to-CPU transfer time decreased from `1.404 s` to `0.671 s` (`52.2%`).

About O_DIRECT alignment, IIUC the blocks in the CPU layer are all of the same size for a model. So the start addresses that we store/load either conform to the alignment requirements of the disk or not. 

I think we can determine this in the manager.py and use the existing `use_o_direct` flag to signal compliance. This should eliminate most of the changes to io.py and fs_io.cpp. 

Reference : https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43689/changes - This PR introduced padding in the CPU layer to align the blocks with `mmap.PAGESIZE` (each CPU row is a block) .
Can we extend/sub-class the file_mapper to support this composition ? That way the manager could be agnostic to the implementation details of the file mapper.

 | Key | Required | Default | Notes |
 | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 | `type` | yes | — | Must be `fs`. |
-| `root_dir` | yes | — | Base directory; vLLM creates subdirectories beneath it (see [On-Disk Layout](#on-disk-layout)). |
+| `root_dir` | yes | — | Base directory, or an ordered comma-separated list of directories with `path_sharding: "by_block_hash"`; vLLM creates subdirectories beneath each one (see [On-Disk Layout](#on-disk-layout)). |
+| `path_sharding` | no | unspecified | Set to `by_block_hash` to distribute complete logical blocks deterministically across multiple `root_dir` paths. |
 | `n_read_threads` | no | `16` | Read-priority I/O threads (load path). |
 | `n_write_threads` | no | `16` | Write-priority I/O threads (store path). |
 | `enable_kv_events` | no | `false` | Publish `BlockStored` KV events (medium `STORAGE`) for successfully stored blocks. Requires KV cache events to be enabled globally. |
 | `locality` | no | unspecified | `LOCAL` or `REMOTE` relative to the publishing vLLM instance. Included in the tier's KV events only when explicitly configured. |
 
 Each thread group prefers its own queue but pulls from the other when its primary queue is empty, so a write-heavy or read-heavy burst won't leave the off-priority queue waiting. Size the totals to your storage's effective concurrency.
 
+For whole-block path sharding, provide comma-separated roots and select the
+stable block-hash strategy:
+
+```json
+{
+  "type": "fs",
+  "root_dir": "/mnt/ps-1/kv,/mnt/ps-2/kv,/mnt/ps-3/kv,/mnt/ps-4/kv",
+  "path_sharding": "by_block_hash",
+  "n_read_threads": 64,
+  "n_write_threads": 64
+}
+```
+
+Each logical block remains one complete file containing every TP worker's KV
+region. Its content hash modulo the number of roots selects one root. Batches
+are grouped by selected root and submitted as parallel I/O tasks, allowing a
+single request containing many blocks to use multiple storage paths. Changing
+the number or order of roots changes the mapping and makes blocks under the old
+mapping unavailable until they are stored again.
+
+The FS tier probes O_DIRECT support across all configured roots with a
+page-sized transfer from a page-aligned buffer. If all roots pass the probe and
+the block size is aligned to the system page size (`mmap.PAGESIZE`), direct I/O
+(`O_DIRECT`) is enabled; otherwise, it falls back to buffered I/O.
+
 #### On-Disk Layout
 
-Under `root_dir`, vLLM creates a subdirectory `<model>_<digest>`, where `<model>` is the model name with `/` replaced by `_` (so HuggingFace IDs like `meta-llama/Llama-3-8B` don't nest), and `<digest>` is a short SHA256 prefix derived from the run configuration (model, block size, parallelism, dtype, etc.). Runs with the same configuration share the same subdirectory; runs with different configurations live side-by-side under the same `root_dir` without colliding.
+Under each `root_dir`, vLLM creates a subdirectory `<model>_<digest>`, where `<model>` is the model name with `/` replaced by `_` (so HuggingFace IDs like `meta-llama/Llama-3-8B` don't nest), and `<digest>` is a short SHA256 prefix derived from the run configuration (model, block size, parallelism, dtype, etc.). Runs with the same configuration share the same subdirectory; runs with different configurations live side-by-side under the same `root_dir` without colliding.
 
 Inside that subdirectory, blocks are sharded across hash-prefix subdirectories to limit directory fan-out:

About O_DIRECT alignment, IIUC the blocks in the CPU layer are all of the same size for a model. So the start addresses that we store/load either conform to the alignment requirements of the disk or not. 

I think we can determine this in the manager.py and use the existing `use_o_direct` flag to signal compliance. This should eliminate most of the changes to io.py and fs_io.cpp. 

Reference : https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43689/changes - This PR introduced padding in the CPU layer to align the blocks with `mmap.PAGESIZE` (each CPU row is a block) .
Can we extend/sub-class the file_mapper to support this composition ? That way the manager could be agnostic to the implementation details of the file mapper.

Thanks for the PR @ekaynar ! Nice speedup 🚀 

I had comments on 2 things mostly, 
 1. Subclass'ing FileMapper so the manager.py stays agnostic. 
 2. direct_io_alignment - A probe on each invocation may not be required. 

PTAL 🙌  Thanks. 

Also can you share the benchmarking commands you were using ? It'd great for reproducibility and in avoiding regressions. 

I do guidellm benchmarks, like 
```
BENCH_RATE="64"
BENCH_MAX_SECONDS="700"
BENCH_RANDOM_SEED="889"
BENCH_TURNS=5
BENCH_PROMPT_TOKENS="4096"
BENCH_PREFIX_TOKENS="10000"
PREFIX_COUNT=$((4 * BENCH_RATE))

DATA="{\"kind\":\"synthetic_text\",\"prompt_tokens\":${BENCH_PROMPT_TOKENS},\"output_tokens\":${out_tokens},\"turns\":${BENCH_TURNS},\"prefix_buckets\": [{\"bucket_weight\": 100, \"prefix_count\": ${PREFIX_COUNT}, \"prefix_tokens\": ${BENCH_PREFIX_TOKENS}}]}"

guidellm run \
              --backend "kind=openai_http,target=http://127.0.0.1:8000,request_format=/v1/completions" \
              --profile "kind=concurrent,streams=${BENCH_RATE}" \
              --constraint "kind=max_duration,seconds=${BENCH_MAX_SECONDS}" \
              --seed "kind=static,value=${BENCH_RANDOM_SEED}" \
              --data "$DATA"
```
with out_tokens set to 1 and 512 for prefill and decode workloads. It'd be nice to verify that we aren't regressing for these workloads. 

Thanks 🙌
